I've read the agreement route. Now checking whether futon1b stores my reply turns, so the route can find the 🈸 paragraph you're answering.The record links your `🈸:yes` turn to the reply it answers (`in-reply-to`), and that reply's 🈸 paragraph can be read from the text. Checking how offers are signed before writing the change.The route change is written. Adding tests for reading 🈸 paragraphs from a reply, then running them.Tests pass: 10 tests, 49 assertions. Lint reports no errors. Loading the change into the running server from master.㊥ (`🈸:yes` now works) `🈸:yes` now records an agreement whenever the reply it answers asks one question. If the route finds no stored offer, it follows your turn's link to the reply you were answering and takes that reply's 🈸 paragraphs as the agent's offer. One 🈸 paragraph is accepted by `yes`. With several, you answer `yes N`. If there are none, the refusal stands. It's live in the server now. I replayed your earlier `🈸:yes` (the one answering "Shall I build that joined model…") and it's now a recorded agreement, `act:7cbed698…`, on the offer minted from that 🈸 paragraph.

㊢ (what changed) Commit `6d579cfe`:
- **`agreement_record.clj`** reads the 🈸 paragraphs out of a reply and builds an offer from them. Each paragraph becomes one numbered option, with the paragraph text as its label. The offer is dated at the reply and keyed to it, so it is minted only once.
- **The agreement route** falls back to that offer only when it would otherwise refuse with `no-visible-offer`. It checks that the reply is this seat's own assistant turn in the same session. It still requires the agent's offer grant, so the route can't make offers for an agent that couldn't make them itself.
- **The mission** M-aif-over-the-operator now notes that the "agents post an offer for each 🈸" item is mostly met from the reading side (commit `e32a2181`).

㊬ (what I checked)
- **Tests:** four new tests, covering one ask, several asks, no ask, and that the minted offer passes offer validation. 10 tests, 49 assertions pass, and clj-kondo is clean.
- **Live:** the two namespaces were reloaded from master, and the agents route still answers 200. The replay took 32 s, most of it waiting on futon1b.

㊟ (two things to know)
- **Earlier refusals stay on record.** The older refusals are still recorded alongside the new agreement. The earlier `🈸:yes` for the held-out test hasn't been replayed. I can do that if you want the record complete.
- **"Informally: yes please" still won't parse.** By design, only `yes` with an optional number or offer id counts, so that ordinary replies don't trigger agreements. So that turn was handled as conversation, not as an agreement.

previous_reply_acts.text: (what the refusal says) The refusal reports a gap in the record, not a problem with your answer. The agreement route (`agreement_record.clj:70`) only looks for stored offer records on this seat. It never reads my reply text. So when I ask "Shall I…?" without also posting an offer, the route finds nothing, logs `no-visible-offer`, and stops. As you say, `🈸:yes` straight after a single "Shall I…?" can only mean one thing. The fault is that the route ignores the text it's answering. I was wrong to describe it as my 🈸 failing to post something.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why it's built that way) Offers were designed as explicit records, made with `POST /api/alpha/offer`, so that an agreement names exactly what was agreed. The mission work item "Agents post an offer for each 🈸" was meant to fill the gap from the agent side, but it relies on every agent remembering to post. In practice none of my asks today posted one, so all your `🈸:yes` answers were refused. Even so, the work went ahead, because I read your yes from the text.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(fix on the reading side) When no stored offer is visible, resolve `🈸:yes` against the agent's previous reply:
- **One 🈸 paragraph:** that paragraph becomes the offer. The route records it, then records the agreement. The evidence is my reply and your turn.
- **Several 🈸 paragraphs:** the answer is ambiguous, as now. You'd answer with the number or offer id.
- **None:** the refusal stays as it is.
